skill.name: test-driven-development
skill.description: Guide feature, bug fix, and refactoring work through test-first red-green-refactor cycles, with focused advice on meaningful tests and minimal mocking.
skill.summary: Apply a strict test-first workflow to features, bug fixes, and refactoring.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The 27 external-command matches are Markdown fences, inline examples, or documented npm test commands, not Ruby or shell execution primitives. The four reconnaissance matches are ordinary testing prose and a local reference. However, the skill repeatedly directs agents to delete implementation code, creating a real data-loss risk without explicit confirmation.

remediation.suggestion: Replace deletion mandates with preserving work, adding regression tests, and requesting explicit confirmation before removing existing code.

content.value_statement: Tests written after implementation can miss defects and confirm the wrong behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a strict red-green-refactor workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guides feature and bug-fix work through red, green, and refactor stages.
Requires verification that each new test fails for the expected reason.
Promotes one observable behavior and a clear name for each test.
Provides TypeScript and npm examples for tests, implementations, and regression fixes.
Reviews mocking choices against documented testing anti-patterns.
Supplies a completion checklist covering failures, passing tests, edge cases, and clean output.
limitations: The skill provides a method, not framework installation or project configuration.
Its command examples assume npm and require adaptation for other test runners.
Its strict workflow may not fit throwaway prototypes, generated code, or configuration changes.
Following the workflow does not guarantee complete requirements, assertions, or test coverage.

use_cases.title: Implement a New Feature
use_cases.description: Define one expected behavior, observe its test fail, add minimal production code, and refactor after the suite passes.

use_cases.title: Fix a Regression
use_cases.description: Reproduce a reported defect with a failing test before making the smallest correction that prevents recurrence.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Design
use_cases.description: Review coupled code, excessive mocks, weak assertions, and incomplete doubles before planning focused test-first improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Learn the TDD Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through test-driven development for [small feature]. Start with one failing test, wait for its result, then propose minimal implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Use TDD to fix [bug] in [project]. Create a minimal regression test that fails for the expected reason, then implement the smallest fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Preventing a reported defect from recurring.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a TDD refactor for [module] while preserving [behavior]. Identify characterization tests, run each red-green step, and keep unrelated changes out of scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improving design without changing observable behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Advanced Test Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [test suite] for weak assertions, over-mocking, incomplete doubles, and missing edge cases. Propose an ordered TDD plan that preserves real behavior and limits mocking.
prompt_templates.scenario: Strengthening a complex suite with focused, behavior-based tests.

output_examples.input: Add three-attempt retry behavior to an asynchronous operation.
output: RED: Add one test proving that two failures are followed by a successful third attempt.
VERIFY: Confirm the test fails because retry behavior is missing.
GREEN: Add only the three-attempt loop required by the test.
REFACTOR: Improve names after the full suite passes.

output_examples.input: Fix a form that accepts an empty email address.
output: Create a regression test expecting an email-required error for blank input.
Confirm the current implementation fails that assertion.
Add the smallest blank-email validation, then rerun all tests.

output_examples.input: Review a test that asserts only that a mocked sidebar exists.
output_examples.output: The assertion proves the mock exists, not that navigation works. Test the real component role or an observable page behavior instead.

best_practices: Run each new test and confirm it fails because the required behavior is missing.
Keep every test focused on one observable behavior with a descriptive name.
Refactor only after the focused test and the full suite pass cleanly.
anti_patterns: Writing production code before observing a relevant test fail.
Changing a valid test only to make the current implementation pass.
Asserting mock details instead of observable behavior from real code.

faq.question: What is red-green-refactor?
faq.answer: Red creates an expected failing test. Green adds minimal passing code. Refactor improves structure while keeping every test green.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It guides test execution, but actual command access depends on the connected tool, project environment, and user permissions.

faq.question: Which test frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: The method is framework-neutral. Examples use TypeScript, Jest-style assertions, Vitest-style mocks, and npm commands.

faq.question: Can I use it with existing untested code?
faq.answer: Yes. Add focused tests for current behavior before changing it, then introduce each new behavior through a failing test.

faq.question: When should I use mocks?
faq.answer: Use mocks only when isolation is necessary. Understand real side effects first, preserve required behavior, and mirror complete data structures.

faq.question: Are there exceptions to strict TDD?
faq.answer: The source allows human-approved exceptions for throwaway prototypes, generated code, and configuration files.
